samples.summary: Remote-change path never clears the image selection, so the new "any offset-shifting mutation clears it" invariant is bypassed by every collaborator edit
samples.evidence: The diff establishes the rule that any mutation shifting offsets must call `clearImageSelectionForMutation()` (editor.ts:1288 and its ~15 call sites). The remote path is the one mutation source that never does: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:378-393` (`store.onRemoteChange`) calls `editor.getDoc().refresh()`, `editor.restoreLocalCursor(...)`, `editor.validateCursorPosition()` and `editor.render()` — none of which touches `selectedImage` (`restoreLocalCursor` at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3917-3931 only moves the cursor and sets the selection range; `validateCursorPosition` at editor.ts:979-987 likewise). A peer inserting or deleting text before the selected image shifts the `(blockId, offset)` coordinate the selection is expressed in. The hardening added in this diff only protects against the block/inline being *gone*: `deleteSelectedImageInline` and `imageSelectionProvider` re-validate with `findImageAtOffset`, which merely asserts that *some* image sits at that offset — so where a remote edit slides a different image onto the slot (exactly the `blockWithTwoImages` scenario the new tests use for local mutations), Cmd/Ctrl+X or Delete removes/copies the wrong image, and the overlay is painted around it beforehand. Fix belongs at the docs-view remote handler (call `editor.clearImageSelection()` there, the same seam the find bar was given at docs-find-bar.tsx:124) or inside `restoreLocalCursor`.

samples.summary: New code comments claim the context menu offers Copy for a click-selected image; the menu only ever sees a text selection, so that consumer does not exist
samples.evidence: `hasSelection = !!editor.getActiveSelection()` (docs-context-menu.tsx:74) and `showCopy = hasSelection` (line 181) key on the *text* selection only. `selectImageInline` (editor.ts:1255-1259) does `selection.setRange(null)` before setting `selectedImage`, so after a click on an image `getActiveSelection()` is null and the menu shows no Copy at all (in read-only it now refuses to open entirely, since `hasClipboardGroup = !readOnly || hasSelection`). Yet editor.ts:1268-1272 and 2599-2604 justify the read-only image click and the focus call with "the context menu now offers Copy" for images, and the branch's own todo (docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-copy-paste-integrity-todo.md:337) states the opposite ("the context menu still offers Copy only for a text selection"). The rationale in the new comments describes a caller that was not updated; either wire `getSelectedImage()` into `hasSelection` or correct the comments.

samples.summary: Image mousedown's stopImmediatePropagation keeps the frontend context menus from closing — now reachable in read-only too
samples.evidence: `handleImageMouseDown` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2662-2663) calls `stopPropagation()`/`stopImmediatePropagation()` on the container in the *capture* phase, so the event never reaches the bubble-phase document listeners at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-context-menu.tsx:126 and packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-table-context-menu.tsx:103 that close the open menu on an outside mousedown. The menu stays open while the click selects an image behind it. This existed for editable mounts, but removing the `if (readOnly) return` at the top of the handler makes it newly reachable for viewers, who are exactly the users the new read-only Copy entry targets.

samples.summary: The in-table context menu still bails on readOnly, so the read-only Copy entry (and the #872 in-cell copy fix) has no menu entry point inside a table
samples.evidence: `DocsContextMenu.handleContextMenu` returns early when `editor.isInTable()` (docs-context-menu.tsx:68), delegating to `DocsTableContextMenu`, whose handler is `if (readOnly) return;` (docs-table-context-menu.tsx:70). The diff makes body Copy available to viewers, but a viewer right-clicking a selection inside a table cell — the very selection this PR taught `getSelectedBlocks()` to serialize (text-editor.ts:3786-3800) — still gets no menu at all. The sibling menu was left out of step with the new read-only clipboard policy.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. The invariant is real and explicitly documented at editor.ts:1261-1292, which enumerates every entry point that must clear the image selection before shifting offsets (plus the three direct-assignment exceptions and the find-bar seam) — the remote path is absent. docs-view.tsx:378-394 is the only remote-change handler in the frontend (grep for onRemoteChange finds only this and yorkie-doc-store.ts:564/579), and it calls refresh/restoreLocalCursor/validateCursorPosition/render, none of which touch selectedImage: restoreLocalCursor (editor.ts:3917-3931) only does cursor.moveTo + selection.setRange, validateCursorPosition (editor.ts:979-987) only relocates a cursor whose block vanished. I enumerated every assignment to selectedImage in editor.ts (2104, 2143, 2320, 2326, 2405, 2425, 2447, 2675, 3944, 3966) — all on local/user paths — and confirmed the editor holds no remote subscription of its own (no docStore/doc subscribe in editor.ts). clearImageSelection has exactly two frontend callers, both in docs-find-bar.tsx:124,133. The repo states the gap itself at packages/docs/test/view/copy-integrity.test.ts:559-561: the remote path 'leaves the image selection untouched'. The added hardening does not close the reported case: deleteSelectedImageInline (editor.ts:2318-2323), imageSelectionProvider (2341-2345) and the render rect lookup (1906-1908) all key on (blockId, offset) and merely assert that SOME image is there, so a remote edit that slides a different image into that slot yields a wrong-image overlay, copy, and delete. In-lane for blast-radius (invariant violated at a site outside the diff) and major: silent wrong-data mutation on a reachable collaborative path. No counterexample exists.

finding.summary: Resize-drag commit still reads the image coordinate through the throwing `doc.getBlock`, the exact hazard this delta hardened everywhere else
finding.evidence: This delta converts `selectImageAt`, `getSelectedImage` and `updateSelectedImage` to `doc.findBlock` because "the selection is a coordinate that can outlive its block ... `getBlock` throws on a missing id". `handleImageResizeMouseUp` holds the same kind of coordinate (`imageResizeDrag.blockId/offset`, captured at mousedown) and at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2538 still calls `const block = doc.getBlock(blockId);` — which throws (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:187) rather than returning undefined. The very next line, `const current = block ? findImageAtOffset(block, offset) : null;` (editor.ts:2539), is a dead guard that shows the author expected the non-throwing contract. Reachable whenever the block disappears while the mouse is still down — a remote peer deleting the paragraph, or a Ctrl+Z (see the related finding on undoFn) — and the throw escapes a document-level `mouseup` listener.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is not present. `handleImageResizeMouseUp` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2520-2569) reads the drag coordinate at line 2547 via `const block = doc.findBlock(blockId);` — the non-throwing variant (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:193-203) — not `doc.getBlock`. The following `const current = block ? findImageAtOffset(block, offset) : null;` (line 2548) is therefore a live guard, not a dead one, and lines 2542-2546 carry an explicit comment giving precisely the stale-coordinate rationale the finding says was overlooked. A full grep of `doc.getBlock(` in editor.ts yields 16 hits (1418, 1444, 1483, 2062, 2121, 2157, 3280, 3316, 3334, 3589, 3605, 3621, 3683, 3710, 3727, 3919), none of which falls inside the resize handlers at 2491-2591; the nearest, 2062, is `clampPos` in `restoreSelectionFromPresence`, an unrelated path. With the asserted `getBlock` call absent, the described throw escaping the document-level `mouseup` listener cannot occur.
